result.rationale: The diff in GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, making selectedCalendar always undefined where the old code returned a real calendar id. The same dead-fallback pattern appears in deleteEvent. This is a verifiable regression introduced by the diff.

judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares against the same falsy externalCalendarId that selected the fallback branch, so the predicate can never match and selectedCalendar is always undefined (the pre-diff fallback to `destinationCalendar.externalId` is gone). Rescheduling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId (legacy references, or events created via the no-credentialId destination path where CalendarManager.createEvent is called without externalId) now calls Google with calendarId undefined and fails, leaving the stale pre-reschedule event on the calendar.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the new fallback is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the fallback branch runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), so it cannot match any real calendar externalId. This makes `selectedCalendar` effectively always `undefined` in the fallback case, removing the previous behavior that used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (now first/primary destination calendar). The same pattern appears in `deleteEvent()` (`calendarId` computation). This is a concrete logic bug introduced by the diff and will cause updates/deletes to target the wrong calendar (or rely on later defaulting), especially for references without `externalCalendarId`.
